# dsh-session-link

DSH web plugin: copy a deep link to the current session and open a session
directly from a URL. Inst
alls as a client bundle in the profile.
## Features

- **Copy session link** — a 🔗 button in the conversation header copies
`<origin>/?session=<id>` for

the current session.
- **Open by URL** — visiting the app with `?session=<id>` in the query string
f
ocuses that session directly.
## Install
From the Git repository (recommended):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart the profile (or the desktop app) and hard-refresh the browser. Uninstall
with `dsh plugin --
profile web remove dsh-session-link`.
## Runtime compatibility

Targets the **0.2 client contract** (DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 and `dsh web`
0.2.x):

- Header actions register through `ctx.slots.register({ name, id, order }, Component)`,
whose return

value is the disposer. The old `ctx.slots.inject(...)` wrapper is
gone.
- Navigation uses `ctx.uiWo

rkspace.openSession(target)`. `ctx.sessions.open(id)`
no longer exists; the opener retries for ~10s

because `openSession` throws
until the target appears in the loaded session catalog.
- The client mo

dule declares only packages that exist in 0.2
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation`, `@deepseek

-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace`).
The 0.1-era `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` row does not exist any

more and
would leave the row waiting forever.

The plugin needs no `session-reference` service and no client→host RPC: the link
is self-contained,

so it also works in a profile where `session-reference` is
disabled.
## Notes

- Client-only feature: the host half is a mount anchor, no host-side state.
- The deep link carries

the session id; opening it in the same browser profile
(localhost server) selects the session in the

on id; opening it in the same browser profile
(localhost server) selects the session in the sidebar.
